newsitem.title: USA: H&R Block tax preparation worldwide rises.
newsitem.headline: H&R Block tax preparation worldwide rises.

text.p: H&R Block Inc said Monday its total worldwide tax preparation volume increased 18.1 percent to $474.7 million from January 1 through February 28, compared to the same period last year.
Volume comprises the tax preparation fees generated by the nearly 10,000 company-owned and franchised offices in the United States, Canada, Australia and Europe.
The company said the total number of returns prepared worldwide during the period rose 7.9 percent to 8.2 million.
Through February, U.S. returns prepared grew 9.7 percent to 7.6 million, while returns received by the IRS declined 2.8 percent, H&R Block said.
But while U S. operations reported strong numbers, H&R Block said international results have been mixed.
Australia, whose tax season ended in October, currently reports a 12.5 percent increase in tax preparation volume, with a 2.8 percent increase in the total number of returns.
In Canada, the number of tax returns prepared through February fell 2.3 percent, while related tax preparation volume increased 8.5 percent, the company said.
Total Canadian refunds discounted declined 17.3 percent, and related volume decreased 15.3 percent, the company said.
H&R Block said the Canadian tax season got a slow start because of the late distribution of wage slips and the company's efforts to tighten criteria for returns eligible for discounts.

In the United States, the number of returns prepared and electronically filed rose 18 percent to 4.3 million through February compared to 1996. The growth is consistent with that seen by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service, which also saw electronic filing increase by about 18 percent for the same period, H&R Block said.

The number of returns filed electronically for taxpayers who prepare their own returns continued an expected decline, falling 6.4 percent, as more of these customers turned to H&R Block for tax preparation as well, the company said.
Overall electronic filing for H&R Block increased to 12.5 percent over last year. Electronic filing fee volume in the United States rose 15.8 percent.

"The tax season got off to a strong start in January, but we were uncertain how much of that was due to milder winter weather than the year before," said Frank Salizzoni, president and chief executive of H&R Block. "The February numbers clearly indicate that we're continuing to have an excellent season."
